subject: FastPay dedicated capacity expansion — term amendment & throughput commitments
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena@fastpay.com>; Marcus Chen <mchen@fastpay.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 1 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal conversation — capacity upgrade proposal

Hi Elena / Marcus,

Congrats on shipping the new fraud-detection pipeline — saw the benchmarks you shared at the demo last week. Per our earlier conversations, I pulled together a straight-forward path to move FastPay from your current 16-GPU reserved pool to a 32-GPU pool at renewal. High level:

- Target go-live: at renewal on 2027-03-01 (we can phase in canary traffic first week)
- Reserved capacity: 32x A100-equivalent GPUs (dedicated pool)
- Throughput guarantee: baseline throughput equivalent to 2.8M tokens/hour (we can convert to requests/sec for your workloads)
- Pricing: see attached draft amendment (high-level numbers below)

Proposed reserved rate (per GPU-hour, billed monthly):
- Year 1 (annual prepay): $6.25 / GPU-hour
- Year 1 (monthly invoiced): $7.10 / GPU-hour
- 60-day proration on activation; burst allowance: +20% capacity for 48 hours once per quarter

Asks from your side: confirmation of billing terms (monthly vs annual prepay), procurement point-of-contact, and whether you need additional SLAs (e.g., stricter p99 latency). I’ve cc’d Dev (solutions) to help with the canary plan.

If useful, we can do a 30-minute call later this week to walk the amendment and throughput numbers.

Thanks,
Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
https://redwood.ai

Attachment: FastPay_Amendment_v2.docx
From: Elena Morales <elena@fastpay.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Chen <mchen@fastpay.com>; Procurement <procure@fastpay.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Feb 2027 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — capacity upgrade proposal

Thanks Dylan — appreciate the quick draft. A few clarifying Qs before we do a call: 

1) Can you break down the per-hour numbers into monthly committed spend for 32 GPUs? I need that for budgeting.
2) Our manifests show 95% of traffic requires p99 < 1200ms for inference. Your throughput guarantee looks promising but we need firm SLOs tied to credits.
3) Procurement: I’m the initial contact, but our procurement lead (procure@fastpay.com) will handle contract language and PO timing. Our internal timeline is to sign amendments by 2027-02-20 to avoid any gaps.

Also, are we able to get a one-time onboarding credit if we commit to annual prepay? That helps offset migration costs.

Elena
Sr. Product Ops, FastPay

On Mon, Feb 1, 2027 at 9:12 AM Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Congrats on shipping the new fraud-detection pipeline — saw the benchmarks you shared at the demo last week. Per our earlier conversations...
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena@fastpay.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 3 Feb 2027 10:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — capacity upgrade proposal

Hi Elena — great questions. Answers inline below and I attached a PDF with the throughput calibration matrix.

1) Monthly committed spend for 32 GPUs (examples):
   - Annual prepay (12 months, invoiced upfront): 32 GPUs * 24 hrs/day * 30 days * $6.25 = $1,440,000 (one-time invoice covering 12 months)
   - Monthly invoiced (no prepay): 32 GPUs * 24 * 30 * $7.10 = $1,636,800 per month

2) SLOs and credits: proposed SLO is 99th percentile latency under stated workload of < 1200ms with a credit band: 5% of monthly reserved spend credited back per 2-hour window of sustained SLO breach beyond 30 minutes, capped at 50% of monthly reserved spend. We can tighten the credit band for annual prepay.

3) Onboarding credit: we can offer a one-time migration credit equal to 5% of the first-year reserved spend if you sign annual prepay.

Dev will help map your request/response sizes to the throughput guarantee. Can you share a sample 1-hour trace and typical concurrency? If you prefer, we can set a call Thursday to review.

Thanks,
Dylan

Attachment: redwood_sla_32gpu.pdf
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Elena Morales <elena@fastpay.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Feb 2027 14:28:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Renewal conversation — capacity upgrade proposal

Looping in from Commercial Strategy — hi Elena, happy to join the call if helpful. A couple of notes from pricing/legal: 

- We can improve the annual-prepay rate to $6.00 / GPU-hour (final) if FastPay signs a 12-month amendment and pays upfront. This is a limited promotional concession tied to FP-2027-061.
- For contractual clarity: we'll add a separate SLA schedule for throughput and p99 latency for the dedicated pool. The SLA will specify test harness, baseline traffic profile, and measurement windows.
- Burst policy: we can formalize a 25% burst for up to 72 hours, once per quarter, for emergency capacity.

I'll prepare a DocuSign-ready amendment and send a link for review. Dylan — can you confirm finance contact to route the invoice to?

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Commercial Strategy, Redwood Inference

On Wed, Feb 3, 2027 at 10:42 AM Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Hi Elena — great questions. Answers inline below and I attached a PDF with the throughput calibration matrix.
From: Elena Morales <elena@fastpay.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Chen <mchen@fastpay.com>, Procurement <procure@fastpay.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Feb 2027 09:32:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — capacity upgrade proposal

Thanks Stephanie and team. The improved pricing looks attractive. A few follow-ups from Procurement & Engineering: 

- We need a stronger operational credit for SLO misses in the first 90 days while we migrate traffic (suggested: 10% of monthly reserved spend for each qualified SLO breach event, capped at 60% for the trial period).
- Throughput measurement: our eng leads want automated telemetry export (CloudWatch/Datadog or S3 deltas) for validation during canary. Can you expose a read-only telemetry feed for our side?
- Procurement asks for standard indemnity language and to confirm Redwood’s SOC2 type II report availability and retention of audit logs for 12 months.

Timeline reminder: to meet our go-live target, we need a signature by 2027-02-20. If we reach agreement this week, procurement will fast-track review.

Elena
Sr. Product Ops, FastPay

On Fri, Feb 5, 2027 at 2:28 PM Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Looping in from Commercial Strategy — hi Elena, happy to join the call if helpful. A couple of notes from pricing/legal...
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena@fastpay.com>, Procurement <procure@fastpay.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 17:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — capacity upgrade proposal

Elena / Procurement team — appreciate the quick turnaround. Per internal alignment we can do the following amendments to finalize: 

- Final annual prepay rate: $6.00 / GPU-hour (12-month term, invoiced upfront)
- Trial-period SLO credits: first 90 days, credit = 10% of monthly reserved spend per qualified SLO breach event, capped at 60% for the 90-day window
- Burst policy: 25% burst for up to 72 hours once per quarter (operational notice required)
- Telemetry: provide a read-only CloudWatch/Datadog telemetry export and an agreed test harness for canary validation (Dev will coordinate hooks)
- Compliance: SOC 2 Type II report and access to redacted audit logs for 12 months — Stephanie will share the package with procurement.

Next steps:
1) I’ve uploaded the updated amendment (FastPay_Amendment_v2.docx) to the Drive link and created a DocuSign envelope: https://www.docusign.com/fastpay/amendment/FP-2027-061
2) Procurement to confirm signature by 2027-02-20 to keep go-live date.
3) Finance contact for invoice routing: Marcus Chen, mchen@fastpay.com.

If that aligns, we’ll generate the final DocuSign and the Finance team will route the annual-prepay invoice when executed.

Thanks everyone — excited to get FastPay onto the expanded pool.

— Dylan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: FastPay_Amendment_v2.docx
